profile.reading:
The First National Bank Technology Center at 201 North 16th Street sits in downtown Omaha as part of the First National Campus, the multi-building headquarters complex of First National of Nebraska, the parent company of First National Bank Omaha, one of the largest privately held banking companies in the United States. The campus's own building directory lists the Technology Center alongside sibling buildings including the First National Tower (the bank's signature high-rise headquarters), First National Plaza, the original First National Bank building, and a separate First National Business Park, reflecting how the bank has grown its downtown Omaha footprint building by building over several decades rather than consolidating operations into one purpose-built data center campus.

Operationally, the Technology Center building is understood to house infrastructure for First National Technology Solutions (FNTS), a managed-IT-services subsidiary of First National of Nebraska. FNTS's own website describes a business built around mainframe hosting, IBM Power systems, hybrid cloud, distributed systems management, and high-performance computing support delivered to outside enterprise clients as well as to First National's own banking operations, but the company's public site is entirely services-oriented and does not publish a facility address, floor plan, power capacity, square footage, or any tier or uptime certification for this or any specific building. That omission is consistent with FNTS's business model: it sells managed IT services and support contracts, not colocation space marketed to prospective tenants who shop on published specifications, so there is little commercial incentive to publish the kind of facility fact sheet a wholesale colocation provider would.

First National of Nebraska itself is privately held rather than publicly traded, which further limits what surfaces about any individual building through financial disclosures. What can be said with confidence, from the bank's own campus materials and independent business listings, is the building's identity, its address in the North 16th Street corridor of downtown Omaha, and its role as the technology arm of a large regional bank rather than as a commercial data center serving outside colocation tenants at scale. Omaha carries a modest but real data center presence tied to its concentration of insurance, finance, and telecom back-office operations, and a bank-owned technology center of this kind is a typical, if quietly run, piece of that local infrastructure, built for the bank's own operational continuity rather than for public-facing capacity marketing.

reading:
First National of Nebraska, Inc. is a privately held, multi-state bank holding company in Omaha and the parent of First National Bank of Omaha, a bank chartered in 1857. It reports roughly 35 billion dollars in assets and around 4,500 employees. It appears in a data centre registry not as a service provider but as an enterprise that runs its own technology estate, and the one building attributed to it here can be identified precisely from the company's own securities filings.

The registry's row is a building of about 68,800 square feet in footprint standing on the block immediately north of Capitol Avenue between 16th and 17th Streets, inside the bank's downtown campus alongside First National Plaza, the FNBO pedestrian tunnels and the bank's child development centre on Chicago Street. First National of Nebraska's Form 10-K405 for the 2001 fiscal year, filed with the SEC in March 2002, states in Item 2 that the Bank leases three Omaha facilities recently built or then under construction for its use, the first of which is a 194,000 square foot Technology Center at 16th and Capitol Avenue. The other two are a 222,000 square foot office building in First National Business Park at 142nd and Dodge and the one million square foot, 40-storey Tower at 16th and Dodge, then expected to complete in 2002. All three were financed through synthetic leases held by trusts, and the filing gives the cost of the buildings under those leases as 294.2 million dollars at the end of 2001, rising to 345.8 million dollars once the Tower completed. The filing describes the purpose of all three as consolidating multiple office locations to improve operating efficiency.

That is the strongest documentation available, and it is a quarter of a century old. First National of Nebraska stopped filing annual reports with the SEC after that 2002 filing, so there is no later Item 2 to check against. The group's managed services arm, First National Technology Solutions, trades as FNTS and says it has served financial services, healthcare, government and enterprise customers for more than 30 years, managing mainframe, IBM Power, distributed, hybrid, public cloud and high performance computing estates from United States based operations. FNTS publishes no facility address, no floor area, no power figure and no audit certification on its public site.

What is genuinely established, then, is that the building is the bank's Technology Center, that it measures 194,000 square feet, and that the bank has occupied it since about 2001. What is not established is that any part of it is a production data hall. The data centre classification in this registry rests entirely on an OpenStreetMap tag added on 20 October 2022 to an otherwise unnamed building outline drawn in 2014, with the name, the operator and a link to the FNTS website added by the same mapper on 25 March 2026. No IT load, utility service size, generator count or white space area has been published by the bank, by FNTS or by any permit located in this pass, and none should be inferred from the building's size.
